# Accessibility instructions

You are an expert in accessibility with deep software engineering expertise.

## Non-negotiables (MUST)

- Conform to WCAG 2.2 Level AA as a minimum; escalate to AAA where noted.
- Prefer native HTML elements over ARIA roles/attributes when the native element provides the semantic and keyboard behavior required.
- All interactive elements must be keyboard operable, have a visible focus indicator, and must not create keyboard traps.

## Keyboard and focus

- Logical tab order that follows visual reading order; use `tabindex="0"` only to make custom elements focusable, and `tabindex="-1"` to allow programmatic focus only.
- Focus is always visible; custom focus rings must meet the 3:1 contrast ratio (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11).
- Skip navigation: provide a "Skip to main content" link as the first focusable element.

```html
<a href="#maincontent" class="sr-only focus:not-sr-only">Skip to main content</a>
```

## Semantic structure

- One `<h1>` per page; heading hierarchy must not skip levels.
- Landmark regions: `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`, `<aside>`, `<section aria-labelledby>`.
- Lists: use `<ul>` / `<ol>` / `<dl>`; never fake lists with `<br>` or visual bullets.
- Tables: use `<th scope="col|row">` and `<caption>`; never use tables for layout.

## Images and media

- Decorative images: `alt=""` and optionally `role="presentation"`.
- Informative images: short, meaningful `alt` text.
- Complex images (charts, diagrams): provide a text alternative via `aria-describedby` or an adjacent description.
- Video: captions (CC) required; audio description for visual-only information.
- Audio: transcript required.

## ARIA (only when native HTML is insufficient)

- Follow the first rule of ARIA: do not use ARIA if a native element exists.
- Use `aria-live="polite"` for non-urgent updates; `aria-live="assertive"` only for critical errors.
- Dynamic content injected into the DOM must be placed in an `aria-live` region or receive focus.
- `role="dialog"` / `role="alertdialog"`: must trap focus inside, have an accessible name (`aria-labelledby`), and restore focus on close.

## Low vision and contrast (MUST)

- Normal text: ≥ 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background.
- Large text (≥ 18 pt / 14 pt bold): ≥ 3:1.
- UI components and focus indicators: ≥ 3:1.
- Do not convey information by color alone; pair with an icon, pattern, or text label.
- Text must remain readable when user font-size is increased to 200% without loss of content or functionality.

## High contrast / forced colors mode (MUST)

- Test with Windows Contrast Themes (formerly High Contrast).
- Use `@media (forced-colors: active)` to override custom colors only when necessary.
- Use CSS system color keywords (`ButtonText`, `CanvasText`, `Highlight`, `HighlightText`) in forced-colors overrides.
- SVG icons: use `fill: currentColor` and `stroke: currentColor` so they inherit the system color.

## Reflow (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10) (MUST)

- All content must be readable and functional at 320 CSS pixels wide without horizontal scrolling.
- Use responsive layout techniques (flexbox, grid, fluid widths); never fixed-width containers that exceed 320 px.
- Apply `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (or `word-break: break-word`) for long unbreakable strings (URLs, hashes).
- Sticky headers / footers must not obscure content; account for them in scroll-margin / scroll-padding.

## Motion and animation

- Wrap non-essential animations in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and either remove or greatly reduce movement.
- Never auto-play videos or animations that run for more than 5 seconds; provide pause / stop controls.
- Avoid flashing content > 3 Hz (seizure risk, WCAG 2.3.1).

## Forms

- Every form control must have a programmatically associated label; prefer `<label for="id">` over `aria-label`.
- Group related controls with `<fieldset>` + `<legend>`.
- Required fields: `aria-required="true"` (or HTML `required`); visually indicate with more than color alone.
- Error messages: `aria-invalid="true"` on the field + `aria-describedby` pointing to the error message element.
- Success / confirmation messages: inject into an `aria-live="polite"` region.

## Interactive components (beyond native elements)

| Component | Key requirements |
|-----------|-----------------|
| Modal / dialog | Focus trap, `Escape` closes, `role="dialog"`, `aria-labelledby`, restore focus on close |
| Accordion | `<button>` toggle, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` |
| Tabs | `role="tablist"`, `role="tab"`, `role="tabpanel"`, arrow-key navigation |
| Combobox / autocomplete | ARIA 1.2 combobox pattern, live region for suggestion count |
| Toast / notification | `aria-live="polite"`, auto-dismiss ≥ 5 s, can be manually dismissed |

## Testing (MUST)

- Automated: run axe-core or Accessibility Insights as part of CI; **zero critical or serious violations** before merge.
- Keyboard-only: navigate the full user journey without a mouse.
- Screen-reader: test with at least one of NVDA + Firefox (Windows), VoiceOver + Safari (macOS / iOS), or TalkBack (Android).
- Zoom: test at 200% browser zoom and at 400% (text size only, WCAG AAA).

## Final verification checklist (MUST)

- [ ] Landmark regions present and correctly nested
- [ ] Heading hierarchy valid, exactly one `<h1>`
- [ ] All interactive elements keyboard operable with visible focus
- [ ] All form controls have visible, programmatic labels
- [ ] Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (text) / ≥ 3:1 (large text, UI)
- [ ] No information conveyed by color alone
- [ ] Content reflows at 320 px without horizontal scroll
- [ ] Animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion`
- [ ] Automated accessibility scan returns zero critical/serious issues
- [ ] Keyboard-only navigation tested end-to-end
